utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dan Saxon for the Prosecution, together with my colleagues Ms. Bronagh McKenna and Ms. Carmela Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in the courtroom. Appearing today for Mr. Perisic are legal assistants Tina Drolec, Milos Androvic, Chad Mair, and our case manager, Daniela Tasic, Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith, and Novak Lukic, myself, as Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon, Mr. Torkildsen. May I just warn you that you are still bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask the usher to give Mr. Torkildsen a hard copy of his report. When I refer to certain paragraphs, I will reference also the number in e-court, but I believe Mr. Torkildsen will find it easier to find it by the number of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, I should like to broach a topic in your report in chapter 3, paragraph 16 onwards. That's the financing of the Yugoslav Peoples' Army in 1991 and 1992. When I refer to a specific paragraph, I will give you the number, but first of all I'd start with a few general questions. Would you agree if I said that the budget of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, but generally speaking that the budget of a state is a public document and that it is always shown in the form of a law?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least I would agree with your first statement that it's a public document that is always shown in the form of a law that I cannot say. But at least these budgets have been shown in the form of a law when it comes to the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and I emphasise that this is the period up to, let's say, 1991, although formally speaking the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was established in 1992, would you agree with me that there was a federal budget as well as republican and provincial budgets?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in the course of 1990, and 1991 especially, the public revenues of the citizens of Yugoslavia provided much less to the federal budget than to the republic budgets?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that -- just trying to make your point of what actually makes up these budgets. The republican budgets, meaning on the republican level, they were, to a large extent, financed by income tax on the citizens, while the federal budgets, they again will be made up by contributions by the socialist republics and the two autonomous regions and the likes of custom taxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know any other sources of revenues to the federal budget? What else financed the federal budget? In paragraph 16 you enumerate these sources specifically. You can look at that paragraph. It lists the sources of the federal budget. Are there any sources that you did not include there in the first sentence?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm here pointing out in paragraph 16 that the customs and import taxes, the contributions, as I mentioned, and also by loans from the National Bank of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know, do you, whether the loans from the National Bank of Yugoslavia before the first half of 1991 were also financed from the primary issue?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely they were, but the magnitude of this financing, meaning the loans and the primary issues, were much less. I have, for instance, also reviewed the SFRY budget, all the annual accounts for 1990, and then the proportion coming from loans or primary issues from the National Bank of Yugoslavia was much less.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I looked up that budget I noticed another source of financing for the budget which you did not include here. Perhaps it's not important. But do you agree that federal taxes were also a source of financing for the federal budget?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I have to posit back. I don't know what type of federal taxes you would be referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Literally, in the budget of the SFRY and later in the budget of the FRY and even Republika Srpska, one of the original sources of financing was the taxes paid by citizens for services rendered by federal authorities, federal agencies. Do you know anything about that? I have to be more precise, because the word "tax" is a bit different from the English word "tax," because in Serbian the word "taksa" means a fee, an administrative or other fee, paid for services rendered by the federal agencies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm very sorry to interrupt, but I have a similar concern as I expressed, I believe, last week. Page 4, lines 6 to 8, Mr. Lukic says: "When I looked up that budget, I noticed another source of financing for the budget which you did not include here. Perhaps it's not important." And then lower down, line 12: "Literally, in the budget of the SFRY and later in the budget of the FRY and even Republika Srpska, one of the original sources of financing was the taxes paid by citizens for services rendered by federal authorities, federal agencies." My concern is simply this: It seems to me that these are statements of fact as opposed to questions, Your Honour. And I don't know what the source of this is or whether the witness can say the source of this, but it's simply a concern that what is coming into the record is somehow not being shown here in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is ambiguous in the record what has or has not been shown to the witness. I put it to the witness because in paragraph 16 he lists item by item what he established to have been the direct revenues to the budget. I'm asking him about another source of direct revenue. If he doesn't know, he doesn't know. I just wanted to remind him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The point is, Mr. Lukic, this is an expert witness. He's not a fact witness, so you are not trying to test his memory whether he knows the facts. If you know of any other source of income, show it to him; let him comment on it. Because he has given us in his report what he has considered to be sources of income, and if you are aware of any other sources of income that is not there, say to him, Are you aware of whether this was another source, and he will say whether he was, and let's see the source. I think the point being made by the Prosecution is that you're making a statement and either the witness believes what you say or he doesn't believe you. But if you confront him with real evidence and say, This is another source; did you consider it, then it's a different story.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with you completely, Your Honours, concerning the documents that I intend to put to this witness, concerning some of my assertions. But I am just testing here some of the claims he made in his report based on his own sources. I don't want to show the documents to him and open some new issues. I will in my case present new documents, whereas here I'm just testing the credibility of the expert witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem that I see is that the testing, at least at this stage, is being done in the form of assertions of fact, rather than questions being put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Assertions of fact, Mr. Lukic, which are not substantiated and this witness, therefore, will not be in a position to comment on those assertions. But your learned friend is making a point. Do you have a response to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. In any case, I will formulate my questions in such a way as to get an answer from the witness. If I don't have a document in front of me, I won't ask questions of that sort.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying, Mr. Torkildsen, that a large deficit in the federal budget in 1991 derived mainly from the fact that the republics had stopped paying their compulsory contributions?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that would be an important reason for the deficit, but it would also be at that time that they had actually started to print money in order to finance the deficit, because when you start printing money, things get out of hand in terms of that the inflation starts to accelerate. And that means that the only option left, if this printing of money continues, is to continue printing money in order to finance this deficit. So it would not only be that the contributions have stopped, but also the fact that you have started to print money in order to -- in order to make up for the budget deficit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Mr. Torkildsen, isn't that a "cause and effect" kind of situation? Isn't the printing of money resorted to because the citizens -- the provinces have stopped contributing, and therefore, there is a deficit because they are not contributing? Therefore, money gets printed to make up the shortfall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the way that I understand it, because there were no other sources of finance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So would you then agree with Mr. Lukic's proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to emphasise, what is the cause and what is the effect. In the next sentence of paragraph 16 you say that increasing disintegration of the SFRY in 1991 adversely affected the budget, especially in the area of revenues. Were you aware that Slovenia and Croatia had stopped paying their contributions to the federal budget even before they had declared their independence?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That sounds natural, yes, that they stopped contributing when they proclaimed independence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. In fact, I asked you whether you knew they had stopped paying contributions even before - before - the declaration of independence.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen any facts to that, but I am -- I assume that what you're saying here is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the same paragraph you refer to the reason for the resignation of Prime Minister Ante Markovic, and you quote a newspaper article regarding his resignation, and this quotation says that as much as 81 per cent of the budget for 1992 was envisaged to finance the JNA. As a percentage it creates the impression that we are talking about a militarist state, seeing how large a proportion of the budget was used for the army. But do you know who the other beneficiaries of the federal budget were?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall from reviewing the documents whether you had established that most of the institutions, such as police, the justice system, the healthcare system, were financed at the republic level? The education system, the pension funds.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may be correct, but today I cannot remember which institutions were financed at the republican level and which institutions were financed at the federal level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just now coming out from that question, my question is: This 81 per cent, was it 81 per cent of the federal budget?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the government led by Mr. Ante Markovic had proposed enacting a law for financing certain requirements of the national defence in September 1991? I believe that's mentioned in the next paragraph, or perhaps a bit further down below.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that. That is actually discussed in, I think, a couple of the other documents that is attached to my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to call up 65 ter 6560.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is the document you referred to in your report and which has not been introduced by the Prosecution. So this is September 1991. A draft law made by the Federal Executive Council, still led by Ante Markovic, a draft law on revenue sources for financing certain requirements of national defence in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to move to the statement of reasons. That's page 4 in B/C/S and page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll read one passage. That's the penultimate paragraph in B/C/S. "As of 26 August 1991, for the financing of the JNA, 27 per cent of the plan for 1991 has been realised from direct revenues." And now on the next page, it says just below these numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page in English and the next one in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "Due to the insufficient in-flow of revenue, problems in financing the JNA have reached a critical point, because in addition to regular expenditures, there have also been considerable extra expenses incurred by the relocation of units and institutions from the territory of Slovenia and the engagement of the JNA in connection with the current crisis in the country." Now, this document that you see in front of you proposed by the federal government, did it follow that session of the Presidency you said took place in August?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I understand it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And after that session of the Presidency, the federal government, called the Federal Executive Council, proposes the enactment of this law to cover the shortfall in the federal budget for purposes of financing the army, to the benefit of the army.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This law was, in fact, enacted; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The writer of this draft law suggests that the deficit be covered from loans from the National Bank of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: These loans stated in this draft law, were they to be from the primary issue?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the law is proposed by Ante Markovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was at least the prime minister for the SFRY at that time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnicity of Mr. Markovic, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was from -- he is from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know by any chance if he remained in Belgrade after his resignation?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I've understood, he left Belgrade after his resignation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's now take a look at another document. It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we get another document, Mr. Lukic, what do you want to do with this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I apologise. I'd like to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If possible, Your Honour, I'd like to propose that the document be tendered, both the proposal and the supplement to the document, both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We've not heard anything about the supplement of the document. I do have a question for you, though --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You asked the witness whether this draft was passed into law. Do we have the law as passed, not in draft form? I think that would be a better exhibit to tender rather than this one, if indeed it was passed into law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honour. I don't have the law with me, but I read that the law was passed in the report. But I'd like this draft to be admitted because there it includes the statement of reasons, explaining the motives for which the government is proposing the law, and I think that's the important point, to understand the motives for the law to be imposed, and that is found in the statement of reasons proposed by the government. But I'm sure I could find the law and then tender that, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. 65 ter 6560 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D10, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd now like to move on to another area and some other documents. You analysed a document which -- just let me take a moment to find it. Let me put it this way: Which means of payment in the Republic of Srpska Krajina existed when it was founded? Were there any changes, any currency changes, that were used in the Serbian Republic of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the documents that I have reviewed, this appears that both the RS and the RSK had their own currency in 1992 and 1993, but I would like to elaborate on that, because their own currency was set at an exchange rate with the FRY dinar at parity, meaning that it could be exchanged on a 1:1 scale. It was fully convertible, meaning that an RSK dinar could be exchanged for one FRY dinar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That currency was also called a dinar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And in the RS, what was it called?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An RS dinar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Also.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's my understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the dinar from Republika Srpska and the Serbian Republic of Krajina? Was it a method of payment, legal tender, throughout Yugoslavia? Could it be used to pay for products?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so, but that would -- I mean, either -- if you could pay in the RS dinar or you actually had to exchange it for a Yugoslav or an FRY dinar first, that I'm not sure about. But the consequences or the result would have been the same in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When did they move on to the Yugoslav dinar in the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: After they introduced the super-dinar that we discussed on Thursday. That would have been from early 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say "super-dinar," and I know what you mean by that. But just to avoid any misunderstanding, that is to say after Mr. Avramovic's programme was passed, that's when the super-dinar came into being; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the monetary system in the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Srpska Krajina, in the legal sense, that they were systems that were regulated as separate autonomous monetary systems, and they had all the necessary legal provisions covered that would cover the monetary system of any state? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we would have to go to the Miletic report that was being referred to on Thursday in order to see the details on that. I can't state that what you are putting to me here is absolutely correct, without looking back at that report to see what is actually stated in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. We'll deal with Miletic's report separately and then you can comment on that as well. We'll do that in due course. But can we agree that the monetary systems, as they were regulated by the provisions in Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina and in the FRY, on the basis of the regulations and everything, were formed and formulated, in fact, in similar fashion, that they were similar?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding, that the whole of the RSK and the RS and the FRY had a similar organisation and it was all tied together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just to avoid misunderstanding with my previous question, I wanted to ask you if you knew that RS and RSK enacted their own laws governing the national bank, currency generally, the payments, and so on. In that sense that's how I saw legal regulations, in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see your point. But also again the documents that I have reviewed also show the total subordination that the national banks of the RS and RSK had for the National Bank of Yugoslavia in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's one of your thesis and we'll deal with that separately. That's one of the things you put forward. We'll discuss it. Now, I am saying that there was a relationship of cooperation during 1992 and 1993 and that after the provisions, or, rather, programme for the reconstruction of the monetary system of the FRY, there was monetary control by the National Bank of Yugoslavia for specific reasons towards the banks of the RS and RSK, but that it was not a relationship of subordination. That's what I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would totally disagree with that. And I would like to refer back to the -- back to the loan that we discussed on Thursday and refer to actually what was stated in there, where it's actually stated that it is the National Bank of Yugoslavia that should determine the use of that loan, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we'll discuss the document, certainly. But you say you don't agree with me; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you, at least not to the full extent of that. They were sort of moving from 1992 and onwards to 1994 in terms of trying to achieve a total integration, and of course they were having their cooperation and so on, but they were moving in the direction of the NBY in Belgrade being in control.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the monetary union is not the same thing as the economic union, that they are two different categories?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That -- that could be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Economic systems between the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the RS and RSK were similar but were not the same; right? Do you agree with me there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, they were -- the economic systems were not -- were not the same basically because the RS, in particular, was from the beginning of the part of the poorest region of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There wasn't a uniform custom system, right, between these three, let me call them, states, but you know what I'm referring to, the three entities, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were no uniform customs system because at least officially the RS and the RSK was not part of the FRY.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They had their revenue from taxes, right, direct revenue from taxes?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We saw that in the budget that we went through on Thursday regarding the 1993 finances, where we saw that the primary issues more or less financed the whole budget. But, of course, I assume that there would be a very small proportion of that coming from direct revenue, like taxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think there might have been a mistake in the interpretation here. Just give me a brief answer. My question was this: Whether there were direct -- whether there was direct revenue from taxes, from customs levies?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: From customs levies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before the witness answers, who are you talking about? Because your first question at line 9, you said: "They had their revenue from taxes, right, direct revenue from taxes?" And who are the "they," if you can just tell us who are the "they"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was thinking of the budgets of the Republika Srpska and the RSK, whether from their own customs they had direct revenue in the budget.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Yes, Mr. Torkildsen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would be correct. A very small proportion would also come from various taxes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There was no uniform price policy either between the FRY and the RS and RSK; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you have to be more specific there, Mr. Lukic. I'm sorry. When it comes to uniform price policy, regarding what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For example, let's look at the prices determined by the state, for example, for cigarettes, fuel, and so on. Excise taxes, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was a uniform pricing system or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There wasn't a uniform system of taxation either, was there?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have on the screens P311, please, the next document. And the page I'd like to look at is -- just let me take a moment to check with the registrar, but I think that only page 12 has been admitted into evidence, or, rather, pages 12 and 13 of this decision but not the entire Official Gazette, just the decision. Yes, that's right. Now can we have it in the B/C/S as well? Page 12 and 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a decision by the Government of Republika Srpska on the use of funds from primary issue, which was passed on the 2nd of June, 1992, or, rather, it was passed on the 14th of May, to be precise, and published in the Official Gazette of Republika Srpska on the 2nd of June, 1992. That's right, isn't it? Now, this decision speaks about the methodology of how the primary issue funds would be used, those funds that would be applied pursuant to this decision of the National Bank of Yugoslavia, the funds that would be released by that decision.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your analysis and in the research you did, did you come across any document of the commercial banks or some state organ, for that matter, which could confirm that this decision was acted upon?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From this decision can we see who the benefits of the primary issue sources was, the beneficiary of the primary issue sources was?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is listed here in Article 1, it's the National Bank of Yugoslavia that -- that should determine the use of this money, according to their decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you misunderstood. Can we see from this decision who is going to use the funds given by the National Bank of Yugoslavia --

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- who's going to benefit from them? Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we have document P314, an MFI document, put up, please. It is a document that I asked you to decide upon its admission after I conduct my cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll do that. Just for my own edification, this Article 1 refers to a common monetary policy and common elements. Do you know, Mr. Torkildsen, what was the common monetary policy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, then I would have to refer back to the Miletic report again where this is outlined. I'm sorry, but I can't state the details regarding that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have P314 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's like this: This is a decision, Mr. Torkildsen, or, rather, I assume that you found this decision in the Prosecution database that you were provided, just like the other documents that you refer to.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You agree with me, I believe -- or, rather, first, can you tell me when this decision was passed? Can you see this on the basis of this document?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see there is a date up in the right-hand corner, mentioning the 8th of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Look at the B/C/S version and you'll see that the date is written in hand there, so it's not a question of you not knowing the language. But anyway, the date that is mentioned in the English version is a hand edition on the B/C/S document, right, written in hand?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this handwriting there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the introduction to the decision, in the preamble, there's a space for the date. There's a dash there and there's no date written in in the space; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. It is mentioned here "4/92" in the first sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we now go on to page 2. Can we see page 2 in both versions, the B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you can see on the original, the B/C/S original, and indeed on the English version, this document has not been signed and there's no government stamp, or any other stamp for that matter; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see no stamp. That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the left-hand corner -- on the left-hand side, there's an empty space for the number; right? We call it the reference number, and all official documents are recorded and then the reference number is written into the document. And you agree here that there's no number here, right, in either version?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, paragraph 5 of this decision says: "The Republic ..." I assume it means Republika Srpska "... and the National Bank shall sign a contract within 30 days from the day this decision comes into force." During your research, did you come across any contract which would be linked to this decision?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically a contract. No, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, Article 6 or paragraph 6 reads as follows: "This decision comes into force on this day and shall be published in the Official Gazette of the Serbian People of Bosnia and Herzegovina." And we saw that the previous government decision that we discussed was, indeed, published in the Official Gazette. Now, during your investigations did you come across this decision having been published in the Official Gazette of RS anywhere?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having seen a decision regarding this, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's just go back for a moment to the first page and see that handwritten edition. May we have the B/C/S version and the English of the first page? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read out what it says there, what the inscription in writing: "Minister Subotic," and then that's underlined, and underneath that line it says: "Coordinate these with the needs of the army," and we have a signature and probably the date. "Coordinate installments with the army." Now, my question is this: From these contents and from that note there, remark there, can you make any conclusions as to whether the decision was passed, or is this just a proposal and remained a proposal?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I get your question, sir. I'm sorry, if you can repeat that, please. I can't -- well, I'm reading the text now, and I can't see whether the -- whether the decision was passed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my question. So from this decision, you cannot establish and ascertain whether the decision was passed and put into force or not; right?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would still like to ask you not to admit this document into evidence. At this point in time I'm challenging both relevancy and authenticity. Now, I can provide the documents later on. Perhaps Mr. Saxon would like to put some questions in the re-direct with respect to his -- with respect to this document, but I think it is just a proposal and not a decision. And the expert witness during his work used this document and said that it was a government decision, but he has now confirmed that he believes that this is a government proposal and not a final decision that was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're saying you'd still like to ask that it not be admitted into evidence. Is it not already P314, or are you saying it's going to be expunged from the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If you recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I've now been told. An MFI. Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document was seized by the Office of the Prosecutor from the archives of the Ministry of Defence of the Republika Srpska in Banja Luka on the 6th of December, 2001. Your Honour, obviously governments keep documents in their archives because these documents record the official business of the government. Whether this was merely a proposal or whether it was a decision that was eventually passed, the point is this was a business record kept by this institution of the Government of Republika Srpska, and so the fact that the government -- the document was kept in the government archives should be sufficient indicia of reliability, at least for purposes of admission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still challenge the relevance of this document because in his work this expert witness analysed the document as being a government decision. But from this document we can't actually see, and I'm claiming that this is, in fact, a draft decision and we cannot know whether there was a decision passed. So I don't see what -- how this document can be of assistance to the Trial Chamber if we don't know whether it was put into effect in any way. And that is why I suggest that either you do not adopt and admit this document because it's not relevant, or if the Prosecution finds that there was a final decision on the basis of this draft, then I won't have anything against it being admitted into evidence ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, an item is relevant if it speaks to an issue that is pertinent in these proceedings, and this document does just that, Your Honour. It speaks to the issue of how the Government of Republika Srpska was financed in 1992. Whether it was simply a proposal or whether it became a final decision, it doesn't change the fact that it is relevant. Quite frankly, Your Honour, on Thursday Your Honour admitted, I believe, other proposals - I can't name the exhibit number - but certainly Your Honour admitted requests, although there is no evidence right now that those were -- those requests were fulfilled. And I submit we are in the same position with this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document will remain marked for identification until -- whether or not you can give us an original -- a final decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I'd like to ask a few questions on the Miletic report. I believe that's P310. No, it's P315, because there have been certain changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your report you analyse it in paragraph 45.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I don't know if the Trial Chamber has Mr. Torkildsen's report in front of them. If not, we should maybe first call up this passage in his report, paragraph 45. It's page 16 in English and 15 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the next stage, and I quote here, from your analysis of the Miletic report. In paragraph 45 you say: "The programme created a single monetary region to include the FRY, the RS, and the RSK. This programme came into effect on the 1st of March, 1994." My first question is: Where did you find this date?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date mentioned here must have come from the report itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have read the whole report, and I haven't found that date anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it would be a good idea to give the witness a hard copy of his -- sorry, the Miletic report, during the break so that we don't have to go through it page by page now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But is this date significant in any way?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is significant in the way that that's from approximately the point in time where the super-dinar was introduced and when they used the same currency across the three entities in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I maintain that the programme of the restructuring of the monetary system and the economic recovery of Yugoslavia was adopted on the 24th of January, 1994, and it entered into force on that day and it was on that day that the super-dinar started to apply. Does that date mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the exact date now, but I'm sure that what you're putting to me in terms of the super-dinar being introduced on the 24th of January, 1994, that that is correct. That sounds right, from what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, the way you analysed the Miletic report, I understood and you will correct me if I'm wrong, so that the third stage of this monetary union between the FRY, the Republika Srpska, and Republika Srpska Krajina, you call it "The Programme of Reconstruction of the Monetary System and the Strategy for the Economic Recovery of Yugoslavia." Is that so? Did I understand your reasoning correctly?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because, quite frankly, I understand it quite differently, this Miletic report. But we'll see. Maybe I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up the Miletic report. In B/C/S, page 2. That's P315. We need page 2 in B/C/S and page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Item 3, Miletic writes: "The period of commencement of the implementation of the reconstruction of the monetary system and the strategy for the economic recovery of Yugoslavia, hereinafter 'programme,' in the part relating to Republika Srpska and the Serbian Republic of Krajina ..." Now, I asked you this last Friday, and I can't remember your answer. The programme of Governor Avramovic that came into effect on the 24th of January, 1994, was called "The Programme of Economic Recovery of Yugoslavia" and not "The Programme of Monetary Union." That's what I maintain. To be more precise, in this part 3, Miletic describes how this programme adopted by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and for the FRY was implemented in the RS and the RSK.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't get your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I maintain, I put it to you that Miletic quotes in his report under number 3, and it's called "The Programme of Reconstruction of Monetary System and the Strategy for Economic Recovery of Yugoslavia" was a programme adopted for the FRY, not for the Republic of Serbian Krajina or Republika Srpska. It's just that they implemented certain parts of it that were relevant to them. It's not about a monetary union of the three entities.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I totally disagree on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you read, let me repeat this, "The Programme of Reconstruction of Monetary System and the Strategy for Economic Recovery"? It's a thousand-page public document.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not read that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know the name of the Avramovic programme, designated, to effect, an economic recovery of the country and the whole system, or do you believe it is a programme destined for all the three entities?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't comment on that 1.000-page programme because I haven't read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Would you agree with me that the gist of the programme for the economic recovery of Yugoslavia, that is, the reconstruction of the monetary system and the strategy for economic recovery, was to stop financing the state by printing money, and thus to stop inflation?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding, without having read the 1.000-page programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And one of the means to reach that end was the introduction of the new dinar, the super-dinar.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose you are very familiar with the Miletic report. And my thesis is that the whole point of this Miletic report was to establish whether the National Bank of Republika Srpska was able to successfully join the Avramovic programme that it would implement in one of its segments.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that applied exclusively to the monetary system, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Miletic report is discussing the monetary system, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And nowhere in the Miletic report do we find the word "subordination"; only the word "cooperation" is used.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that means I would have to look through the Miletic report. It's one thing that you are using the word "subordination" as such. The other thing, if there are certain facts described in the report that is actually speaking about subordination without using the term, again, I would have to look at the report in detail in order to answer that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection to the witness reviewing the Miletic report during the break, if the Trial Chamber agrees, so that he can answer this question. Before the break, just a few brief questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In a monetary union, is it the case that the one who prints money and makes it available to another, is it normal for the former to have control over the flow of monies so that the interests and the existence of the money printer are not jeopardised?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will ask you even more simply: Legally, in contractual relations, is it important for the lender to ensure that the borrower is credit-worthy, solvent, so that the loan be eventually repaid?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In normal circumstances that would be the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By introducing the new dinar, hyperinflation was completely stopped; isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my understanding. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if this new super-dinar had been used without any control, that would have been running the risk of a new round of hyperinflation in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it's a good time for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Lukic. We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Torkildsen, let us now go back to the two questions I asked earlier regarding the Miletic report. One, did you see in the Miletic report the word "subordination" or any reference to a relationship of subordination between the National Bank of Yugoslavia on the one hand and the National Banks of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina? Did you find any references that would indicate such a relationship?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to answer the first part of your question, I did not see the word "subordination" being used in the translation at all, but I did find references within this Miletic report that actually describes the relationship of subordination, and I would like to point out page 3, paragraph 4, in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it possible to have it on the screen, or is it part of your report, Mr. Torkildsen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What I can do is to read out the relevant paragraph, if it is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is stated here that: "The competent institutions of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina would bring all other regulations on which the implementation of the agreed single monetary and credit policy depended on into line with regulations adopted by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia." And then I would like to point out at -- also, paragraph 5, on the same page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you like to read that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. "Monetary policy projections for certain periods and their provision were carried out in accordance with the relevant elements in the programme and were brought into line with the relevant portions of the quantitative tasks of the monetary policy carried out by the National Bank of Yugoslavia. "In this context, it is especially worth mentioning that the quantity frameworks for the amounts of dinars that the National Bank of Republika Srpska issued to the banks from the area of Republika Srpska were also brought into line by relevant decisions of the National Bank of Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you kindly slow down for the interpreters. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry. "They are established in accordance with the valid set of instruments and valid decisions of the National Bank of Yugoslavia." Sorry, I made a note of this during the break and now I was referring to page -- page 4, I think, but I actually meant to start referring on page 3. I just need to find -- back to that. Sorry about this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. The fourth paragraph on page 3, this is actually what I made a note of now during the break and not what I just referred to. "The National Bank of Republika Srpska and the National Bank of the Republic of Serbian Krajina would bring all monetary and credit regulation instruments in line with relevant monetary and credit regulation decisions of the National Bank of Yugoslavia." And then I would, in particular, like to highlight the paragraph on the bottom here. "All necessary changes resulting from the achieved monetary and credit movements would be agreed upon through standard expert cooperation and through decisions taken at a meeting of national bank governors, which would then be verified at sessions of national bank boards." And then the question then arises, and I would like to refer back to the document that we pointed out last Thursday regarding the voting rights concerning these meetings, and where it was in particular pointed out that the voting rights not being there for the National Bank of the RS and the RSK. And I would also like then to go further on to page 4, the first paragraph, where it is stated. "The corner currency reserving of the National Bank of Republika Srpska and the National Bank of the Republic of Serbian Krajina would be a constituent part of the foreign currency reserves of the National Bank of Yugoslavia, to be kept on the books as special accounts abroad and subsidiary accounts of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. The National Bank of Yugoslavia would issue orders for the use of foreign currency reserves from the National Bank of Republika Srpska and the National Bank of the Republic of Serbian Krajina through the relevant national bank." It is basically stated here that it is the National Bank of Yugoslavia who's going to determine how the foreign currency reserves of the National Bank of Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina should be used, and in my view that is -- that is a good example of subordination in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to follow up on the last thing you said. The foreign exchange reserves of the National Bank of Republika Srpska, did they serve as collateral for obtaining dinars from the National Bank of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding from -- from -- from the period after approximately February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the National Bank of Yugoslavia able to dispose of this foreign exchange monies it had deposited with it without the consent of the National Bank of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way that I read this, that it was up to the NBY in Belgrade to determine the use of this foreign currency, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's your interpretation from what you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more clarification on what you've said a moment ago when you said that the representatives of the National Banks of Republika Srpska and the RSK attended the sessions of the Board of Governors of the National Bank of Yugoslavia without having voting rights. You were referring to another document, not the Miletic report; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Miletic report, quite the opposite is written. It describes how decisions were made in the National Banks of Republika Srpska and the RSK. There is no mention of any interference in the decision-making of the Board of Governors of the National Bank of Yugoslavia in monetary issues. That's the passage that refers to expert assistance.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not specifically mentioned, anything about the voting rights in the Miletic report. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 3 in English. We need to look at the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The last paragraph stipulates the method of decision-making concerning monetary policy; correct.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's mentioned here, "standard expert cooperation" and "through decisions taken at the meeting of national bank governors."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it says in English: [In English] "... credit movements would be agreed upon through standard expert cooperation."

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Let me remind you of another question I put to you earlier concerning the date, the 1st of March, 1994, mentioned in your report. Did you see it anywhere in the Miletic report, or alternatively, did you remember why you wrote it in your report?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I checked the document, and I could not find a specific date, as you pointed out, within the report. I would just like to add to that, and that is that this Miletic report, when I reviewed this, was part of a bundle of other financial documents, a total of six documents, and I have at least not invented those dates myself. So that means that those dates must come from one of the five other documents that was contained within that bundle of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to move to page 8 in B/C/S of the same document and page 9 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S, towards the middle of the page, it says: "Finally, as a very important segment in the implementation of the programme, there remains the question of regulating real direct revenues of the budget of Republika Srpska. In this area the National Bank of Republika Srpska is in constant contact with the competent authorities of Republika Srpska with which this issue needs to be regulated in line with the intentions of the programme." Do you agree that this paragraph, and, indeed, the whole report, does not mention anywhere that the collection of direct revenues by Republika Srpska would be in any way connected with the FRY?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's now move to another document. It's an MFI, and again it was decided that the Trial Chamber will decide on admission after my examination. P323, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an Official Note dated 12 May 1994, and you refer to it several times in your report and you mentioned it again when you spoke about the relationship of subordination. You agree, correct, that's the document on the basis of which you claim there was a relationship of subordination between the National Bank of the FRY and the National Banks of Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, if this is the document mentioning the issue of no voting rights and also other -- other issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You found this document in the Prosecution's collection of documents when you were doing your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, please, or, rather, page 3, the last page of the document. It's a three-page document. In fact, the English version has five pages and the B/C/S has three.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see who the author of this document is? I don't know if you heard the question.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you, can we see from this document who authored it? Can you conclude who the author is?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't read the signature on the last page, if that is a signature at all, unless it is stated in the beginning of the document, the author.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, in view of the contents of this document, would it be standard procedure for this document to be signed, have a stamp and reference number, if it's an Official Note made at a kind of important meeting, that seems to be the case from the introduction?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether that would be standard procedure, I wouldn't know. But since it's an Official Note, it wouldn't be unlikely at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, we are still discussing this document because I have new problems with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 65 ter 6526. That's P315. In English we need page 13, and in B/C/S, page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the document which, as you said earlier, you reviewed together with the Miletic report, that there were many of them, and they have the same 65 ter number. I maintained that this document is absolutely identical to the previous one in terms of substance. I don't know how best to deal with this, if we can return to the English version of the previous document for you to compare. There are only certain differences in the format.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we put the English version of the previous document alongside?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, have a look at these two documents, or perhaps you've done it before during your own research. The language is absolutely the same. Perhaps there are certain differences in the English translation, but do you think it's the same substance?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assumed at the time that I reviewed these documents that it was the same document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, I'm sorry about complicating the work of the registrar. I'd like the B/C/S version of the previous document and the B/C/S version of the current one, the last page. Leave the first page for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read what it says in B/C/S because it's a problem for me. This Official Note, which is of the same substance as the previous one, is written in a different dialect. Unfortunately, that's not -- this is the one. Right. In the document on the left, and the interpreters can confirm this, it says "Official Note" with the word "beleska" used, and the document on the right is called "Official Note" with the word "zabiljeska" used and it's written in the Ijekavian dialect. Maybe you weren't able to establish this, but perhaps you had a language assistant helping with you. This dialect is not written in Serbia. If you don't know, just say so, we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. And in general terms, I can't testify to the authentication of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at just the last pages of both documents. That's page 3. We've seen this one. And now I'd like to see the last page of the zabiljeska document, in B/C/S. The other document. P315, the last page. Thank you. That's it. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can see there is a difference in the ending. On the right-hand side, I will read it in Serbian, it says, "The Governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia ..." and it's not signed. My question is: When you were reviewing the Official Note of Mr. Miletic, you said that attached to it you saw a whole group of other documents; correct?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Actually, it was, if I remember correctly, five other documents, but they were not attached to the Miletic report as such. But it was filed with the Prosecution's evidence system as a complete batch of documents, but I always viewed these documents as being separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was precisely my problem when I had certain doubts on Thursday regarding the date quoted in Miletic and the date of this Official Note. It's part of a set of documents but it's obviously not related to the report. You don't know who the source is of this document on the right-hand side, which has "Governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia" at the bottom? You know nothing of the providence of this document, do you?

utterances.speaker: MORTEN TORKILDSEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I still stand by the arguments I presented earlier. I don't know how clear a picture I succeeded in drawing for you, but before us we have two documents, both unsigned, absolutely the same in substance but written in different dialects. I suppose it is indeed -- both documents are indeed from the database of the Prosecution, but we cannot ascertain the authenticity because even the expert witness cannot tell us who authored it, and we know nothing else that could corroborate its authenticity. The document tendered by the Prosecution is P315, MFI, and they did not tender this other one, probably to avoid complications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, let me just make sure that I'm following everything that is happening. Am I right in saying, in fact, it's not only two documents here, but there are three? I thought before you called the document on the right side of the screen, there was another document here in B/C/S with a signature or a handwriting similar to the one on the left. So it will be those two with their handwritings plus this one on the right. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are -- there is a total of two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The registrar has answered my query. Thank you so much. You may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could hear the arguments that my colleague wishes to put forward. I have said why I think the document is not an authentic one. Perhaps he can take the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's correct that the Prosecution has tendered what is now MFI P323. The Prosecution did not see the need to tender both documents. Your Honour, the fact that both documents are substantively the same is an indication of their authenticity because they corroborate each other. Can we turn, please -- for the document on the left, we see what looks like it's an illegible signature in the bottom left-hand corner. Can we turn back to the first page, please. This document, Your Honour, MFI P323, was seized from Mr. Orsat Mijenic, who on the 25th of July, 2001, was the head of the Government of Croatia's Office for Cooperation with the Hague Tribunal. You'll see here in the upper right-hand corner, it contains -- let me start with the left-hand corner. I'm apologising. I'm messing up my left and right. In the upper right-hand corner, there are clerical notes. Do you see the letters "12.05" and then "1994," indicating that this document has been formally processed. This document is on the letterhead of the National Bank of Yugoslavia, and as I said before, it contains what appears to be a signature at the end, albeit illegible. Those, Your Honour, should be sufficient indicators of reliability and authenticity for the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, now that brings me to an even greater problem. I now have greater problems with authenticity since it is from the Government of the Republic of Croatia, since I don't see how they could come into possession of this document. That's my first point; and secondly, what it says there is a memorandum, not a stamp. It's not the reference number of the National Bank of Yugoslavia. It's an Official Document - the expert can tell us about that - issued by the National Bank of Yugoslavia, has the letterhead, memorandum, stamp, and the number -- the reference number of the document. So this reinforces my doubts about this document. And the fact that it exists in Ijekavian, which is the other dialect used in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia, that version of the Serbian language, and written in the Cyrillic adds to my confusion and tells me that all this is problematic, and I challenge the authenticity on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honour, the fact that the OTP received this from the Government of Croatia, again, is an indicator of its authenticity. At the time this document was produced in May 1994, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and Croatia were at war, thus there can be many reasons why the Government of Croatia might have obtained this document, and certainly the Government of Croatia thought the document was important enough to keep in its possession until 2001 when it turned it over to the Office of the Prosecutor, pursuant to a request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, I have a slight problem. Your submissions, at page 40, starting at line 4 to line 16, constitute in my prima facie view essentially some kind of testimony, rather than argument. But be that as it may, I'm not holding it against you because obviously you are doing your best to come to the rescue of the Chamber, and the Chamber does not understand Cyrillic or B/C/S. But be that as it may, our guidelines on the admission and presentation of evidence and the conduct of counsel in court, at paragraph 34, read as follows, and I would like to, in the light of your objection, to give guidance to the Chamber as to what to do. "There is no general prohibition on the admission of documents simply on the grounds that their purported author has not been called to testify. Similarly, the fact that a document is unsigned or unstamped does not a priori render it void of authenticity." That is the guideline we have all agreed to go by, and I would imagine that where a document is unsigned and unstamped, if it shows relevance to the issues before the Court, we could accept it. What do you say we should say, given those guidelines?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am fully conscious of your guidelines, Your Honour, and you will recall that a large number of documents were admitted here during the proceedings so far that didn't take the form that I am presenting now and the Defence made no opposition to that large number of documents, because we considered that the contents of the documents were such that we were not in a position to challenge their authenticity. But looking at the format and form of this document, although it fulfills the conditions set down by the guidelines which would allow you to accept its authenticity, because of the facts that I just presented, I still challenge its authenticity. Now, I would like the translation service perhaps to be called in to a assist, if this is still a problem and you don't wish me to testify, that the CLSS can give you their positions, stating whether they are substantively the same text, provided in two different forms, if that would help you. I know that you have to weigh up the validity of the documents, if you accept their authenticity or not. But as I have just learnt from the Prosecutor, except from the fact that they received it from the Government of the Republic of Croatia, I cannot establish whether the document is truly authentic. The doors have just been closed. So could we retain the MFI and then perhaps the Prosecutor can tell me more exactly about the source of the document and then we can establish its authenticity better later on, in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you may, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What I find inconsistent, Your Honour, with the Defence's position, for example, just one example, on Thursday the Trial Chamber, without any objection from the Defence, admitted Exhibit P315. That is the Miletic report which, as far as I can see, has no stamp or signature. And I don't understand why we're in a different situation with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess we're in a different situation with this document, Mr. Saxon, because, as you say, the Miletic report is the Miletic report, so the author is Miletic, so it is known who the author is. That may make the difference. But I don't know why they objected -- they didn't object, rather, to that one. At this stage, Mr. Lukic, what I wanted to ask you before Mr. Saxon stood up was, you are now suggesting that we go to CLSS to clear the problem. I didn't get the feeling, or the impression, rather, from your objection that you are challenging the substance of these documents. In fact, I thought your submission was that the substance was the same, with slight language differences, but that they are talking to the same issues. So I do not think that referring these documents to CLSS will resolve our problem. Therefore, I am not quite sure whether you have responded pertinently to the problem that I have posed, that the guidelines say we can admit an unsigned, unstamped document, as long as it is relevant, because when I put that to you, you then raised the question of CLSS. I don't know whether you would like to respond to that again, or is that the end of your argument?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have no problem as far as the CLSS is concerned, as long as -- I see you've understood what I'm saying, that it is substantively the same where it says the governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia in one document, but not in the other, but the contents are the same. Now, with respect to the guidelines is my doubt. Looking at the format of this document, I am challenging its authenticity, but I am fully conscious of the fact that it can be admitted into evidence as it stands, even if the form doesn't correspond fully to what it should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you are aware of that, then may -- I think we should then admit the document. Obviously, the Chamber will give whatever weight it gives to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, you must excuse me. What document is this? Is this P315, MFI?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the Miletic report?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I help?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I believe this document is P323 that was marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is not 65 ter 6526, which you called P315, MFI, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What Mr. Saxon just said, that's the note proposed by the Prosecutor, and it had the MFI number. So I now agree to having the document admitted, but I'd also like to propose, Your Honours, that we admit the other document, the one we compared it to, so that you have both documents before you when you come to weigh up the two, and that is part of ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you finish your sentence, then I'll respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know where the problem is, Your Honour, the problem, as we see it, and I really do not wish to complicate matters. The problem is that it's 315 is Miletic's report; that's in e-court. The entire document, 80 pages long, within the frameworks of which you will find this to, and as far as I understood your decision, it was that only Miletic's report, 10-page report, be admitted. So that's why the whole issue has been complicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You've confused me even further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm advised P315 is the first ten pages of the Miletic report. P323 is the Official Note. Now, where I sit, I am assuming that what we have on the screen are the two versions of the Official Note; therefore, what we have on the screen is P323. What I don't know is which of these versions is actually P323, MFI, because the one you proposed now to tender so that we can compare, but I would like to be certain which one is already P323, MFI, between these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the document, the MFI document, which is on the left-hand side of the screen. To be precise it has the ERN number 0207-6891.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That is P323, MFI. And you are saying yes, we can now admit it into evidence. May it then be admitted into evidence as an exhibit P323.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit status of P323 will be changed, Your Honours, accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fine. Now, the other one on the right-hand side you now wish to tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Prosecution does not object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then shall be give it a D exhibit number, please? It is admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
